audit_status.source_base: Greek 1 Corinthians text tradition, draft aligned to public-domain comparison layer later
audit_status.review_note: Compact complete draft reviewed for servants/stewards, judgment, not beyond what is written, apostolic humility, fatherly admonition, kingdom in power.

verses.restored: Let a human calculate us this way: as attendants of Messiah and stewards of mysteries of the Divine.

familiar.text: Let a man so account of us, as of the ministers of Christ, and stewards of the mysteries of God.

modern.text: So then, men ought to regard us as servants of Christ and stewards of the mysteries of God.

original.text: Οὕτως ἡμᾶς λογιζέσθω ἄνθρωπος ὡς ὑπηρέτας Χριστοῦ καὶ οἰκονόμους μυστηρίων θεοῦ.

verses.restored: Here, furthermore, it is sought among stewards that one be found trustworthy.

familiar.text: Moreover it is required in stewards, that a man be found faithful.

modern.text: Now it is required of stewards that they be found faithful.

original.text: ⸀ὧδε λοιπὸν ζητεῖται ἐν τοῖς οἰκονόμοις ἵνα πιστός τις εὑρεθῇ.

verses.restored: But to me it is a very small thing that I should be examined by you or by a human day; indeed I do not even examine myself.

familiar.text: But with me it is a very small thing that I should be judged of you, or of man’s judgment: yea, I judge not mine own self.

modern.text: I care very little, however, if I am judged by you or by any human court. In fact, I do not even judge myself.

original.text: ἐμοὶ δὲ εἰς ἐλάχιστόν ἐστιν, ἵνα ὑφʼ ὑμῶν ἀνακριθῶ ἢ ὑπὸ ἀνθρωπίνης ἡμέρας· ἀλλʼ οὐδὲ ἐμαυτὸν ἀνακρίνω·

verses.restored: For I am conscious of nothing against myself, but I have not been made righteous/just by this; the one examining me is the Lord.

familiar.text: For I know nothing by myself; yet am I not hereby justified: but he that judgeth me is the Lord.

modern.text: My conscience is clear, but that does not vindicate me. It is the Lord who judges me.

original.text: οὐδὲν γὰρ ἐμαυτῷ σύνοιδα, ἀλλʼ οὐκ ἐν τούτῳ δεδικαίωμαι, ὁ δὲ ἀνακρίνων με κύριός ἐστιν.

verses.restored: Therefore judge nothing before the season, until the Lord comes, who will both bring to light the hidden things of darkness and make manifest the counsels of hearts; and then praise will come to each from the Divine.

familiar.text: Therefore judge nothing before the time, until the Lord come, who both will bring to light the hidden things of darkness, and will make manifest the counsels of the hearts: and then shall every man have praise of God.

modern.text: Therefore judge nothing before the appointed time; wait until the Lord comes. He will bring to light what is hidden in darkness and will expose the motives of men’s hearts. At that time each will receive his praise from God.

original.text: ὥστε μὴ πρὸ καιροῦ τι κρίνετε, ἕως ἂν ἔλθῃ ὁ κύριος, ὃς καὶ φωτίσει τὰ κρυπτὰ τοῦ σκότους καὶ φανερώσει τὰς βουλὰς τῶν καρδιῶν, καὶ τότε ὁ ἔπαινος γενήσεται ἑκάστῳ ἀπὸ τοῦ θεοῦ.

verses.restored: These things, siblings, I transferred to myself and Apollos because of you, so that in us you may learn not beyond what has been written, so that no one is puffed up for one against another.

familiar.text: And these things, brethren, I have in a figure transferred to myself and to Apollos for your sakes; that ye might learn in us not to think of men above that which is written, that no one of you be puffed up for one against another.

modern.text: Brothers, I have applied these things to myself and Apollos for your benefit, so that you may learn from us not to go beyond what is written. Then you will not take pride in one man over another.

original.text: Ταῦτα δέ, ἀδελφοί, μετεσχημάτισα εἰς ἐμαυτὸν καὶ ⸀Ἀπολλῶν διʼ ὑμᾶς, ἵνα ἐν ἡμῖν μάθητε τό· Μὴ ὑπὲρ ⸀ἃ ⸀γέγραπται, ἵνα μὴ εἷς ὑπὲρ τοῦ ἑνὸς φυσιοῦσθε κατὰ τοῦ ἑτέρου.

verses.restored: For who distinguishes you? And what do you have that you did not receive? But if you received it, why boast as though not receiving?

familiar.text: For who maketh thee to differ from another? and what hast thou that thou didst not receive? now if thou didst receive it, why dost thou glory, as if thou hadst not received it?

modern.text: For who makes you so superior? What do you have that you did not receive? And if you did receive it, why do you boast as though you did not?

original.text: τίς γάρ σε διακρίνει; τί δὲ ἔχεις ὃ οὐκ ἔλαβες; εἰ δὲ καὶ ἔλαβες, τί καυχᾶσαι ὡς μὴ λαβών;

verses.restored: Already you are filled; already you became rich; apart from us you reigned. And would that you did reign, so that we also might reign with you.

familiar.text: Now ye are full, now ye are rich, ye have reigned as kings without us: and I would to God ye did reign, that we also might reign with you.

modern.text: Already you have all you want. Already you have become rich. Without us, you have become kings. How I wish you really were kings, so that we might be kings with you!

original.text: Ἤδη κεκορεσμένοι ἐστέ, ἤδη ἐπλουτήσατε, χωρὶς ἡμῶν ἐβασιλεύσατε· καὶ ὄφελόν γε ἐβασιλεύσατε, ἵνα καὶ ἡμεῖς ὑμῖν συμβασιλεύσωμεν.

verses.restored: For I think the Divine displayed us, the apostles, last, as condemned to death, because we became a spectacle to the world, both to messengers and to humans.

familiar.text: For I think that God hath set forth us the apostles last, as it were appointed to death: for we are made a spectacle unto the world, and to angels, and to men.

modern.text: For it seems to me that God has displayed us apostles at the end of the procession, like prisoners appointed for death. We have become a spectacle to the whole world, to angels as well as to men.

original.text: δοκῶ ⸀γάρ, ὁ θεὸς ἡμᾶς τοὺς ἀποστόλους ἐσχάτους ἀπέδειξεν ὡς ἐπιθανατίους, ὅτι θέατρον ἐγενήθημεν τῷ κόσμῳ καὶ ἀγγέλοις καὶ ἀνθρώποις.

verses.restored: We are foolish because of Messiah, but you are wise in Messiah; we are weak, but you are strong; you are honored, but we dishonored.

familiar.text: We are fools for Christ’s sake, but ye are wise in Christ; we are weak, but ye are strong; ye are honourable, but we are despised.

modern.text: We are fools for Christ, but you are wise in Christ. We are weak, but you are strong. You are honored, but we are dishonored.

original.text: ἡμεῖς μωροὶ διὰ Χριστόν, ὑμεῖς δὲ φρόνιμοι ἐν Χριστῷ· ἡμεῖς ἀσθενεῖς, ὑμεῖς δὲ ἰσχυροί· ὑμεῖς ἔνδοξοι, ἡμεῖς δὲ ἄτιμοι.

verses.restored: Until the present hour we both hunger and thirst, are poorly clothed, are struck, and wander homeless,

familiar.text: Even unto this present hour we both hunger, and thirst, and are naked, and are buffeted, and have no certain dwellingplace;

modern.text: To this very hour we are hungry and thirsty, we are poorly clothed, we are brutally treated, we are homeless.

original.text: ἄχρι τῆς ἄρτι ὥρας καὶ πεινῶμεν καὶ διψῶμεν καὶ γυμνιτεύομεν καὶ κολαφιζόμεθα καὶ ἀστατοῦμεν

verses.restored: and labor, working with our own hands. Being insulted, we bless; being persecuted, we endure;

familiar.text: And labour, working with our own hands: being reviled, we bless; being persecuted, we suffer it:

modern.text: We work hard with our own hands. When we are vilified, we bless; when we are persecuted, we endure it;

original.text: καὶ κοπιῶμεν ἐργαζόμενοι ταῖς ἰδίαις χερσίν· λοιδορούμενοι εὐλογοῦμεν, διωκόμενοι ἀνεχόμεθα,

verses.restored: being slandered, we encourage/appeal. We became as refuse of the world, scum of all things, until now.

familiar.text: Being defamed, we intreat: we are made as the filth of the world, and are the offscouring of all things unto this day.

modern.text: when we are slandered, we answer gently. Up to this moment we have become the scum of the earth, the refuse of the world. Paul’s Fatherly Warning

original.text: ⸀δυσφημούμενοι παρακαλοῦμεν· ὡς περικαθάρματα τοῦ κόσμου ἐγενήθημεν, πάντων περίψημα ἕως ἄρτι.

verses.restored: I do not write these things shaming you, but admonishing you as my beloved children.

familiar.text: I write not these things to shame you, but as my beloved sons I warn you.

modern.text: I am not writing this to shame you, but to warn you as my beloved children.

original.text: Οὐκ ἐντρέπων ὑμᾶς γράφω ταῦτα, ἀλλʼ ὡς τέκνα μου ἀγαπητὰ ⸀νουθετῶν·

verses.restored: For though you may have ten thousand guardians in Messiah, yet not many fathers; for in Messiah Jesus through the good news I fathered you.

familiar.text: For though ye have ten thousand instructors in Christ, yet have ye not many fathers: for in Christ Jesus I have begotten you through the gospel.

modern.text: Even if you have ten thousand guardians in Christ, you do not have many fathers; for in Christ Jesus I became your father through the gospel.

original.text: ἐὰν γὰρ μυρίους παιδαγωγοὺς ἔχητε ἐν Χριστῷ, ἀλλʼ οὐ πολλοὺς πατέρας, ἐν γὰρ Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ διὰ τοῦ εὐαγγελίου ἐγὼ ὑμᾶς ἐγέννησα.

verses.restored: Therefore I urge you: become imitators of me.

familiar.text: Wherefore I beseech you, be ye followers of me.

modern.text: Therefore I urge you to imitate me.

original.text: παρακαλῶ οὖν ὑμᾶς, μιμηταί μου γίνεσθε.

verses.restored: Because of this I sent to you Timothy, who is my beloved and trustworthy child in the Lord, who will remind you of my ways in Messiah, just as I teach everywhere in every assembly.

familiar.text: For this cause have I sent unto you Timotheus, who is my beloved son, and faithful in the Lord, who shall bring you into remembrance of my ways which be in Christ, as I teach every where in every church.

modern.text: That is why I have sent you Timothy, my beloved and faithful child in the Lord. He will remind you of my way of life in Christ Jesus, which is exactly what I teach everywhere in every church.

original.text: διὰ τοῦτο ἔπεμψα ὑμῖν Τιμόθεον, ὅς ἐστίν ⸂μου τέκνον⸃ ἀγαπητὸν καὶ πιστὸν ἐν κυρίῳ, ὃς ὑμᾶς ἀναμνήσει τὰς ὁδούς μου τὰς ἐν Χριστῷ ⸀Ἰησοῦ, καθὼς πανταχοῦ ἐν πάσῃ ἐκκλησίᾳ διδάσκω.

verses.restored: Some were puffed up as though I were not coming to you.

familiar.text: Now some are puffed up, as though I would not come to you.

modern.text: Some of you have become arrogant, as if I were not coming to you.

original.text: ὡς μὴ ἐρχομένου δέ μου πρὸς ὑμᾶς ἐφυσιώθησάν τινες·

verses.restored: But I will come to you quickly, if the Lord wills, and I will know not the word of those puffed up but the power.

familiar.text: But I will come to you shortly, if the Lord will, and will know, not the speech of them which are puffed up, but the power.

modern.text: But I will come to you shortly, if the Lord is willing, and then I will find out not only what these arrogant people are saying, but what power they have.

original.text: ἐλεύσομαι δὲ ταχέως πρὸς ὑμᾶς, ἐὰν ὁ κύριος θελήσῃ, καὶ γνώσομαι οὐ τὸν λόγον τῶν πεφυσιωμένων ἀλλὰ τὴν δύναμιν,

verses.restored: For the reign of the Divine is not in word but in power.

familiar.text: For the kingdom of God is not in word, but in power.

modern.text: For the kingdom of God is not a matter of talk but of power.

original.text: οὐ γὰρ ἐν λόγῳ ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ θεοῦ ἀλλʼ ἐν δυνάμει.

verses.restored: What do you will? Shall I come to you with a rod, or in love and a spirit of gentleness?

familiar.text: What will ye? shall I come unto you with a rod, or in love, and in the spirit of meekness?

modern.text: Which do you prefer? Shall I come to you with a rod, or in love and with a gentle spirit?

original.text: τί θέλετε; ἐν ῥάβδῳ ἔλθω πρὸς ὑμᾶς, ἢ ἐν ἀγάπῃ πνεύματί τε πραΰτητος;

translation_notes: Paul's father-language is pastoral and rhetorical; it should not be inflated into domination.
The kingdom/reign in power contrasts performative speech and puffed-up status with Spirit-backed reality.
